params.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Halt detection: the ground speed below which a sampled reading cannot be told from a complete cessation of movement, set by the speed resolution of vehicle-tracking data. It is the tolerance the concept drv.motion.standstill takes, and it bounds nothing about the adequacy of any conduct.
params.source: Speed-sensor and object-tracking resolution conventions in naturalistic-driving and simulator datasets.

params.name: p.backing_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Backing detection: the magnitude of the velocity component along the heading below which a sampled reading cannot be told from no motion along the heading, set by the resolution of velocity in vehicle-tracking data. It is the tolerance the concept drv.motion.backing takes.
params.source: Speed-sensor and object-tracking resolution conventions in naturalistic-driving and simulator datasets.

params.name: p.corner_window
params.convention: Low-speed manoeuvre recognition: the window over which the heading change of a reversing vehicle is integrated, taken as the time a passenger car needs to reverse through a right-angle corner at typical backing speeds (a quarter-circle of radius about one and a half vehicle lengths at 2 m/s).
params.source: Low-speed vehicle manoeuvre geometry (AASHTO Green Book design-vehicle turning paths for the passenger car, driven in reverse).

params.name: p.corner_heading_change
params.convention: The magnitude of heading change that distinguishes backing around a corner from backing straight or with ordinary steering correction: half of the quarter turn a street corner subtends, so that a corner manoeuvre is recognized once it is half completed while a kerbside correction is not.
params.source: Turning-manoeuvre classification thresholds used in naturalistic-driving trajectory coding.

params.name: p.corner_reach
params.convention: The reach within which a junction region counts as the corner the subject is backing around: the ground distance from the body outline to the junction, taken as the length of the corner return plus a design vehicle's length.
params.source: Intersection corner radii and design-vehicle lengths (AASHTO Green Book).

params.name: p.approach_view_sight_distance
params.convention: Departure sight triangle for a stopped passenger car turning onto or crossing a two-lane highway: the length of intersecting highway that must be visible in each direction, taken as the distance a vehicle at the highway's design speed covers in the time the stopped vehicle needs to depart (about 7.5 s at 50 km/h).
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, intersection sight distance (Case B, stop control on the minor road).

params.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
params.convention: Stop-point tolerance of the ontology's approach convention: the bound within which a halt counts as made at the named place, set by the positional accuracy of mapped line and crosswalk geometry together with the body-outline reference, so that a halt within measurement noise of the mark is read at it.
params.source: Map-matching and GNSS positional accuracy conventions for lane-level road geometry.

params.name: p.against_direction_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Direction-of-travel detection: the magnitude of the velocity component along a region's designated direction below which a sampled reading cannot be told from no motion along that direction, set by the resolution of velocity in vehicle-tracking data. It is the tolerance the concept drv.motion.travels_against_region_direction takes.
params.source: Speed-sensor and object-tracking resolution conventions in naturalistic-driving and simulator datasets.

params.name: p.under_way_yaw_rate
params.convention: Yaw resolution: the magnitude of yaw rate above which a body counts as changing its heading at this observation, set just clear of the noise floor of a tracked heading so that an observation inside a turn is told from one before it began; it names the source's resolution and no measure of how sharp a turn must be.
params.source: Tracking convention: the yaw-rate noise floor of object tracks travelling straight.

params.name: p.turn_window
params.convention: Low-speed manoeuvre recognition: the window over which the heading change of a turning vehicle is integrated, taken as the time a vehicle takes to sweep a junction-sized turn at approach speeds, long enough to contain the whole sweep and short enough not to run two manoeuvres together.
params.source: Intersection turning-path and manoeuvre-duration figures of the geometric design convention (turning paths of the design passenger car).

params.name: p.turn_heading_change
params.convention: The magnitude of heading change that tells a turn from lane keeping, from following a bend and from the yaw of a lane change: half a right angle, above the heading change of road curvature and of lane changes at road speeds and below the quarter turn of an ordinary junction turn.
params.source: Manoeuvre-classification thresholds of naturalistic driving studies (turn versus lane-change discrimination by heading change).

params.name: p.through_region_window
params.convention: Manoeuvre recognition across a junction: the window over which the heading change of a body crossing a junction-sized region is integrated, taken as the time a vehicle takes to traverse such a region at approach speeds, long enough to span the whole passage.
params.source: Intersection traversal times of the geometric design convention (junction width over approach speed).

params.name: p.through_region_max_heading_change
params.convention: The magnitude of integrated heading change at or below which a body counts as having held its course across a region rather than turned out of it: below the yaw of a junction turn and above the yaw of lane keeping and of the skew of junction legs that meet at other than right angles.
params.source: Manoeuvre-classification thresholds of naturalistic driving studies (through movement versus turn by heading change).

params.name: p.heading_alignment_cosine
params.convention: Direction-agreement resolution: the cosine above which a normalised heading counts as aligned with a region's designated direction, set just clear of zero so that any heading within a right angle of the designated direction counts and only the source's own resolution in heading and in the written direction is excluded. The words name no angle; they name the roadway designated for the direction travelled, so the parameter carries resolution only and no measure of adequacy.
params.source: Map-matching convention: heading-to-link agreement tolerances of lane and link matching.

params.name: p.cautious_reaction_time
params.convention: Perception-reaction time of a driver already halted and watching the junction it is entering, shorter than the 2.5 s of an open-road stopping-distance model because the hazard is the one the driver has stopped to look for.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book brake-reaction time, reduced to the expected-hazard case of intersection manoeuvres.

params.name: p.cautious_deceleration
params.convention: Deceleration a driver is comfortable with and most road surfaces allow, the figure the stopping-distance model of the geometric design convention uses.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book deceleration rate for stopping sight distance.

params.name: p.cautious_min_clearance
params.convention: The centre-to-centre closest approach below which a projected passage counts as a conflict rather than a clearance, taken as the standing separation of the gap-acceptance convention.
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual gap-acceptance clearance; surrogate safety conflict definitions.

params.name: p.cautious_horizon
params.convention: Conflict-horizon convention: the time over which a constant-velocity projection of two bodies is taken to hold at junction speeds, the horizon of the surrogate-safety time-to-conflict measures.
params.source: Surrogate safety assessment time-to-collision horizons (the 3 s threshold of conflict studies).

params.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
params.convention: Conflict-horizon convention: the time over which a constant-velocity projection of two bodies is taken to hold at junction speeds, the horizon of the surrogate-safety time-to-conflict measures.
params.source: Surrogate safety assessment time-to-collision horizons (the 3 s threshold of conflict studies).

params.name: p.yield_min_clearance
params.convention: The centre-to-centre closest approach below which a projected passage counts as impeding the other road user rather than clearing it, taken as the standing separation of the gap-acceptance convention.
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual gap-acceptance clearance; surrogate safety conflict definitions.

params.name: p.yield_forced_decel
params.convention: The deceleration beyond which a road user counts as having been forced to brake for another rather than adjusting its speed at will, taken as the comfortable deceleration of the stopping-distance convention: braking harder than that is an evasive action and not a free choice.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book deceleration rate for stopping sight distance, used as the threshold of evasive braking in conflict studies.

params.name: p.oncoming_direction_cosine
params.convention: The cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed that still counts as approaching from the opposite direction, taken as thirty degrees, which admits the opposed legs of junctions that meet at other than right angles and the yaw of a vehicle already turning while excluding the crossing legs.
params.source: Junction-leg geometry of the design convention: opposing approaches within thirty degrees of opposed.

params.name: p.hazard_time_to_conflict
params.convention: The time separation at which an approaching vehicle counts as an immediate hazard to a manoeuvre across its path: the critical gap a driver accepts for a left turn across oncoming traffic, measured as the oncoming vehicle's distance to the junction divided by its own speed, so the hazard reaches farther up the road the faster the vehicle comes.
params.source: NCHRP gap-acceptance critical gaps for left turns across opposing traffic.

params.name: p.hazard_horizon
params.convention: Conflict-horizon convention: the time over which a constant-velocity projection of two bodies is taken to hold at junction speeds, the horizon of the surrogate-safety time-to-conflict measures.
params.source: Surrogate safety assessment time-to-collision horizons (the 3 s threshold of conflict studies).

params.name: p.hazard_min_clearance
params.convention: The centre-to-centre closest approach below which a projected passage counts as a danger of a crash rather than a clearance, taken as the standing separation of the gap-acceptance convention.
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual gap-acceptance clearance; surrogate safety conflict definitions.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_base
params.convention: Basic-speed-rule convention: the speed a dry, clear, wide, straight and uncongested highway carries, taken as the design speed of a rural arterial, 65 mph = 29.1 m/s. It is the bound from which every condition-dependent reduction of the operationalization is taken, and no condition raises it.
params.source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, design speeds for rural arterials; the general statutory maxima of NRS 484B.627.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_reference_lane_width
params.convention: The standard lane width of highway geometric design, 12 ft = 3.6 m. The base bound is scaled by the ratio of the observed lane width to it, the ratio capped at one, so a narrower way lowers the bound in proportion to its narrowing and a wider one does not raise it.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book standard lane width; the lane-width adjustment of free-flow speed in the Highway Capacity Manual.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_wet_reduction
params.convention: Wet-pavement speed adjustment: the amount by which the bound falls where the surface is wet or rain or snow is falling, taken as 10 mph = 4.5 m/s, the reduction road-weather guidance gives for rain and wet pavement.
params.source: FHWA Road Weather Management speed-reduction guidance; AASHTO wet-pavement friction factors.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_ice_reduction
params.convention: Winter-surface speed adjustment: ice or packed snow leaves roughly half the friction of dry pavement, so the bound falls by about half the base speed, 30 mph = 13.4 m/s, where the surface is icy or snow-covered.
params.source: FHWA Road Weather Management guidance for snow and ice; AASHTO friction factors for icy surfaces.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_darkness_reduction
params.convention: Night-driving adjustment: low-beam headlamps light some 50 to 75 m of road ahead, well short of the daylight sight distance, so the bound falls by 10 mph = 4.5 m/s in darkness.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book headlamp sight distance; FHWA night-visibility guidance.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_per_road_user
params.convention: Speed-flow convention: free-flow speed falls as the traffic stream thickens. The bound falls by this much for each further road user of the traffic within the interaction reach, so the bound moves with how much traffic there is rather than with its mere presence.
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual speed-flow relations for basic freeway and arterial segments.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_traffic_reach
params.convention: The stretch of highway, ahead and behind, within which another road user of the traffic stream interacts with the subject and so counts towards the traffic the bound reads; beyond it a road user on the same way does not bear on the subject's speed.
params.source: Car-following and speed-flow interaction distances of the Highway Capacity Manual.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_reaction_time
params.convention: Stopping-distance model: the perception-reaction time of a driver on an open road, the interval during which the vehicle covers ground at its present speed before any braking begins.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance, 2.5 s brake reaction time.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_deceleration
params.convention: Stopping-distance model: the deceleration a driver is comfortable with and most road surfaces allow, used for the braking part of the distance needed to stop from the observed speed.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance, 3.4 m/s2 deceleration.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_lateral_acceleration
params.convention: Curve-speed convention: the lateral acceleration a vehicle may develop on a bend before its speed counts as improper for the curvature, taken as a side-friction factor of about 0.15 g.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book side friction factors for horizontal curves.

params.name: p.u_turn_window
params.convention: Reversal recognition: the window over which the heading change of a direction reversal is integrated, long enough to span a turning 'accomplished by one continuous movement or not', that is a three-point turning with a halt and a backing movement in it, at the manoeuvre times of low-speed turning.
params.source: Low-speed turning and three-point turn durations of vehicle manoeuvre studies.

params.name: p.u_turn_heading_change
params.convention: The magnitude of integrated heading change at which the body's direction of travel counts as reversed: a half turn less the tolerance an integrated yaw rate carries over a long window and the skew of a way that is not straight, so that a turning onto a way that doubles back is caught and an ordinary quarter-turn junction turn is not.
params.source: Manoeuvre-classification thresholds of naturalistic driving studies (U-turn detection by integrated heading change).

params.name: p.slowing_decel_tolerance
params.convention: Longitudinal-acceleration resolution: the magnitude of deceleration below which a sampled reading of a vehicle's acceleration along its heading cannot be told from travel at a steady speed, about a thirtieth of gravity, the noise floor of differentiated speed traces.
params.source: vehicle-dynamics instrumentation practice for differentiated wheel-speed and inertial traces

params.name: p.curvature_resolution
params.convention: Map-geometry resolution: the horizontal curvature above which a recorded carriageway centreline is distinguishable from a straight one - a radius of about a thousand metres - below which polyline fitting cannot tell a bend from digitising noise. It names only what the source can resolve and imposes no size of bend.
params.source: road-centreline mapping and curvature-estimation practice

params.name: p.crest_reach
params.convention: Crest-approach reach of the geometric-design sight-distance model: the distance ahead of a crest within which a vehicle at highway speed has its view over the crest restricted and cannot stop short of it, the stopping-sight-distance order of magnitude at 80 to 90 km/h. It is the reach within which a recorded crest counts as the one the road user is approaching or near.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping-sight-distance and crest-curve tables

params.name: p.junction_turn_yaw_rate
params.convention: The rate of change of heading at which a body counts as turning at a junction rather than holding its course across it: a vehicle sweeping the quarter turn of an ordinary junction at approach speeds turns through ninety degrees in some three to nine seconds, so its rate is well above this figure, while the heading variation of keeping a lane, correcting a line or following a bend of the road stays below it. It bounds the recognition of the turn and nothing about the adequacy of any conduct.
params.source: Intersection turning-path and manoeuvre-duration figures of the geometric design convention, with lane-keeping heading variation from naturalistic-driving data.

params.name: p.oncoming_lookback
params.convention: The window behind the observation within which a vehicle that was approaching from the opposite direction still counts as the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction, taken as the time a vehicle takes to sweep a junction-sized left turn at approach speeds: over that sweep the subject's own heading rotates a quarter turn away from the opposed direction, and the duty is owed throughout the manoeuvre the words bind.
params.source: Junction turning-manoeuvre duration of the geometric design convention (the sweep of a left turn at approach speeds), the same span as the turn-recognition window of the manoeuvre concepts.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_floor
params.convention: Crawl-speed floor of the basic-speed-rule convention: the speed below which no combination of surface, weather, light, width and traffic conditions makes a vehicle's rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, taken as the slowest speed the jurisdiction's own speed law posts, 15 mph = 6.7 m/s. It floors the condition bound of the operationalization, so that the summed condition reductions never bring the bound to or below nothing and never condemn a vehicle standing still or creeping; the stopping-distance and curve bounds need no floor, since both hold of themselves at rest.
params.source: NRS 484B.363 school-zone speed limit, the lowest limit the jurisdiction's speed law posts; AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, minimum design speeds for low-speed urban streets.

params.name: p.adjacent_portion_width
params.convention: The width of the portion of the right half of a way beside its centre line where the source records no lanes and so no division of the half: the standard lane width of highway geometric design, 12 ft = 3.6 m, the width one line of vehicles occupies, so that the strip next to the centre line is as wide as the lane a laned way would mark there. The offset compared against it is taken from the road user's reference point, as `prim.region_lateral_offset` defines it.
params.source: highway geometric design practice (the 12-foot standard lane width)

params.name: p.following_reach
params.convention: The longitudinal distance ahead within which a vehicle counts as the one being followed: the car-following interaction range, beyond which a leader no longer constrains a follower, taken as the distance covered in about four seconds at highway speed. It is the reach the concept drv.interaction.following takes and decides nothing about adequacy.
params.source: Car-following interaction ranges in traffic-flow theory (Highway Capacity Manual).

params.name: p.following_same_direction_cosine
params.convention: The cosine of the largest heading difference that still counts as travelling in the same direction, taken as twenty degrees - the heading spread of vehicles keeping a lane through a curve or a correction. It is the tolerance the concept drv.interaction.following passes to rel.same_direction.
params.source: Lane-keeping heading deviation distributions in naturalistic-driving data.

params.name: p.follow_headway_base
params.convention: The minimum time headway on a dry road of the standard following convention: the perception-reaction time of an alert driver plus a margin, so that the follower can begin braking before closing the gap the lead's braking opens.
params.source: The 'two-second rule' of driver-handbook and highway-safety practice; perception-reaction time of 1.5 s in AASHTO stopping-sight-distance practice.

params.name: p.follow_headway_wet
params.convention: The addition to the minimum headway on a wet surface or in falling rain or snow: the standard doubling of the dry following time where the surface friction available for braking is reduced by water.
params.source: Driver-handbook wet-road following practice; reduced wet-pavement friction coefficients in highway design guidance.

params.name: p.follow_headway_ice
params.convention: The addition to the minimum headway on an icy or snow-covered surface: the further extension to the order of eight to ten seconds that winter-driving practice requires, reflecting friction on ice of roughly a fifth of dry pavement.
params.source: Winter-driving guidance of state departments of transportation; ice friction coefficients in vehicle-dynamics practice.

params.name: p.follow_headway_per_vehicle
params.convention: The addition to the minimum headway for each further road user of the traffic stream within reach on the highway: with denser traffic a lead's braking is more likely to be abrupt and the room to escape to either side is lost, so the required headway rises with the count.
params.source: Car-following and traffic-density headway distributions in highway capacity practice.

params.name: p.follow_traffic_reach
params.convention: The reach along the highway within which other road users count as 'the traffic upon the highway' for the subject: the stretch within which another user's manoeuvre can reach the subject before it can react, taken as the distance covered in about four seconds at highway speed.
params.source: Traffic-conflict observation reaches used in naturalistic-driving studies.

params.name: p.caravan_max_gap
params.convention: The longitudinal gap within which a road user counts as travelling close behind another in a line: about four vehicle lengths, the spacing a procession holds to keep its line intact and to be seen as one group. It is a recognition reach of the concept drv.interaction.caravan and decides nothing about the space the law requires.
params.source: Platoon spacing observed in escorted and ceremonial processions; jam-spacing multiples in traffic-flow theory.

params.name: p.caravan_same_direction_cosine
params.convention: The cosine of the largest heading difference between members that still counts as travelling in the same direction, taken as twenty degrees.
params.source: Lane-keeping heading deviation distributions in naturalistic-driving data.

params.name: p.caravan_min_followers
params.convention: The number of road users travelling close behind another, besides the one at the head, at which a line counts as a procession rather than two road users happening to travel together: a group of at least four, the platoon size traffic-flow theory recognizes as a travelling group.
params.source: Platoon definitions in traffic-flow theory (four or more vehicles travelling together).

params.name: p.caravan_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Halt detection within the line: the ground speed below which a sampled reading cannot be told from a complete cessation of movement, so that a halted queue is not read as a line in motion.
params.source: Speed-sensor and object-tracking resolution conventions in naturalistic-driving and simulator datasets.

params.name: p.merge_space_length
params.convention: The length of body that must fit in the space: the design passenger car's length in highway geometric design, the vehicle the words contemplate entering and occupying the space.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book design vehicle P (passenger car) dimensions.

params.name: p.merge_space_clearance
params.convention: The standing clearance left at each end of the entering body once it is in the space: the minimum bumper-to-bumper separation of stationary gap-acceptance practice, applied at the nose and at the tail.
params.source: Minimum vehicle spacing in queueing and gap-acceptance practice (jam spacing less vehicle length).

params.name: p.merge_headway_time
params.convention: The accepted-gap headway: the time separation a merging driver accepts at either end of the space, so the bound grows with the speed of the line as a gap-acceptance criterion does.
params.source: Critical gap values for lane-change and merge manoeuvres in the Highway Capacity Manual.

params.name: p.turn_signal_lead_time
params.convention: Signal-lead convention: the time a signal must have been showing before the movement begins for a driver in the region moved into to have seen and acted on it, taken as the perception-reaction time of an alert driver of the standard stopping-distance model. The words require that the signal 'has been given' before the movement and state no length; this is the shortest lead at which a signal is a warning rather than an accompaniment.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book perception-reaction time for an alert driver (the 2 s figure of driver-response models).

params.name: p.lane_change_min_clearance
params.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the standing bumper-to-bumper clearance a driver leaves between its body and another when it has taken a space, the minimum separation of the car-following convention.
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual car-following and gap-acceptance jam-spacing clearance.

params.name: p.lane_change_horizon
params.convention: Conflict-horizon convention: the time over which a constant-velocity projection of two bodies is taken to hold at road speeds, the horizon of the surrogate-safety time-to-conflict measures.
params.source: Surrogate safety assessment time-to-collision horizons (the 3 s threshold of conflict studies).

params.name: p.course_change_window
params.convention: Low-speed manoeuvre recognition: the window over which the heading change of a vehicle leaving its course is integrated, taken as the time a turn at a junction or a movement from one lane to the next takes at ordinary road speeds.
params.source: Naturalistic-driving manoeuvre segmentation practice.

params.name: p.course_change_heading
params.convention: Lane-change kinematics: the magnitude of integrated heading change at which a departure from a straight course is told from lane keeping and from the heading variation of following a bend - a movement from one lane to the next on an ordinary road produces a heading deviation of this order, and a turn at a junction far exceeds it. It is the bound this subsection's act asks for, which covers any turning of a vehicle from a direct course.
params.source: Naturalistic-driving lane-change and turn kinematics studies.

params.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cosine
params.convention: The cosine of the largest heading difference that still counts as travelling in the same direction while passing, taken as thirty degrees — the heading spread of a vehicle pulling out and running abreast during a pass. It is the tolerance drv.interaction.overtaking passes to rel.same_direction.
params.source: Lane-change heading deviation distributions in naturalistic-driving data.

params.name: p.conditions_permit_min_speed
params.convention: The speed above which a heavy vehicle can open and hold a long gap without it being filled: the lower edge of free-flow operation on a two-lane highway, below which traffic is in the stop-and-go or platooned regime and a five-hundred-foot space cannot be maintained.
params.source: Level-of-service speed bands for two-lane highways in the Highway Capacity Manual.

params.name: p.u_turn_max_heading_change
params.convention: The upper bound of the reversal band the concept `drv.motion.u_turn` takes: the magnitude of integrated heading change beyond which what the window carries is no longer a reversal but a turning carried round past the opposite direction, taken as a half turn plus the tolerance an integrated yaw rate carries over a long window and the skew of a way that is not straight - the mirror of the recognition bound `p.u_turn_heading_change`, so that a reversal observed a little past the opposed heading is still denoted while a body come round a full circle, which ends travelling in the direction it set out in, is not.
params.source: naturalistic-driving U-turn kinematics; the band the concept's own challenge record uses

_fields.params: name (p.<name>), value (number), unit (m|s|m/s|m/s2|deg|deg/s|ratio|count), convention (text), figure_review (optional: why a value that equals a figure some law states is a convention, not that figure)
_fields.aggregates: word (a legal aggregate such as 'vehicle'), classes (ru.* ids it covers)

declarations.meaning: The trace declares, for the way a road user is travelling on at this observation, that a public authority has designated it a through street or through highway (traffic on it is not required to stop or yield at the intersections it crosses).

The trace declares, for a road user and a region, that the source's current plan for that road user at that region is to turn to the left there. It is the source's declaration at this observation and not the road user's motion: a turn the plan still holds is declared though it is blocked or not yet begun, and a plan the source does not know is absent rather than false.

The trace declares, for the stretch of way a road user is on at this observation, that the way lies outside the territorial limits of every incorporated city. The declaration is of the administrative boundary of the territory, which no feature on the road displays.

The trace declares, for the stretch of way a road user is on at this observation, that the stretch lies within a business district: territory contiguous to and including the way, built up along it with buildings in use for business or industrial purposes to the frontage the jurisdiction's definition states. Declared false, the stretch lies outside any such district. The declaration is of the administrative character of the territory, which no feature on the road displays.

The trace declares, for the stretch of way a road user is on at this observation, that the stretch lies within a business district or within a residential district: territory contiguous to and including the way, built up along it to the frontage the jurisdiction's definitions state with buildings in use for business or industrial purposes, or with dwellings. Declared false, the stretch lies within neither. The declaration is of the administrative character of the territory, which no feature on the road displays.
